facts.fact: The Star reports that 76 police stations in and around Nairobi had their Occurrence Books digitised by 30 June 2023, with the Deputy Inspector General of Administration Police telling the President the service planned to roll it out to other parts of the country; no total of stations is given.

The Interior Cabinet Secretary said on 30 June 2023 that the police OB had been digitised so that complaints, statements and details of criminal activities made at police stations are recorded in it and cannot be edited.

The Deputy Inspector General of Administration Police said on 30 June 2023 that reports entered in the digital OB at the station are open to monitoring by ward, county and regional commanders and the Inspector General, and the Cabinet Secretary called it real-time reporting of crimes.

The digital OB was presented on 30 June 2023 by the Interior Cabinet Secretary and the Deputy Inspector General of Administration Police as the government's own digitisation, with most personnel said to be trained; no funder or budget is stated.
